query.intent: Surface new Indian AI regulatory requirements and related official guidance relevant to advising OpenAI on its artificial-intelligence activities.

findings.title: Press Release:Press Information Bureau
findings.why: PIB publishes the Government’s account of the legal and platform-accountability framework addressing AI-generated deepfakes, including recent IT Rules amendments and responsible-AI projects.
findings.snippet: The Government remains conscious of the threats posed by deepfakes powered by Artificial Intelligence (AI), including synthetic audio, video and text.

findings.title: Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau
findings.why: PIB publishes an official explanation of the strengthened framework for AI-generated deepfakes, including labelling, metadata, platform due diligence and takedown timelines.
findings.snippet: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team also regularly issues guidelines on AI-related threats and countermeasures, including deepfake; shares safety and security tips and awareness posters, info-graphics and videos on its official websites and social media handles and is aimed at sensitizing internet users on cyber security attacks and frauds including online safety measures for children.

findings.title: BCI issues social media guidelines for advocates, law students - India Legal
findings.why: Reports a Bar Council of India circular imposing professional and educational controls relevant to AI-generated content, deepfakes, confidentiality and digital ethics in the legal sector.
findings.snippet: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has issued comprehensive guidelines regulating the use of social media by advocates, law students and law interns, while making it mandatory for all future applicants seeking enrolment as advocates to submit an affidavit or compliance undertaking affirming adherence to digital ethics and professional standards.

findings.title: AI training, fair dealing and copyright infringement by AI platforms: Analysing Delhi High Court's order in ANI Media v. OpenAI
findings.why: Provides practitioner analysis of the Delhi High Court’s July 2026 ruling on copyright, LLM training, jurisdiction and OpenAI’s Indian users.
findings.snippet: On July 24, 2026, Justice Amit Bansal of the Delhi High Court delivered a judgment that may likely be a foundational stepping stone towards the establishment of an analytical framework on how the Indian judiciary could approach copyright disputes involving the training of large language models (LLMs).

notes: search note: Searches covered Indian government, parliamentary, judicial, regulatory, legal-sector and practitioner sources for developments dated 2026-07-06 through 2026-09-04.

search note: No additional standalone India-wide AI statute or comprehensive AI-specific regulation, apart from the identified synthetic-content/deepfake framework and related governance measures, was located in the searched non-excluded sources.
search note: No results from cert-in.org.in, trai.gov.in, or their subdomains are included.
